projects.title: Multimodal RAG
projects.short_description: A side project for trying out retrieval-augmented generation: add PDFs, Word files or Google Docs, ask questions in your own words, and get answers that cite the pages they came from. A React Native app for iOS, Android and web over a Fastify API with Postgres, pgvector, Claude and Voyage.
projects.long_description: A side project where I try out retrieval-augmented generation end to end. You add PDFs, Word files or Google Docs and ask questions in your own words. Claude reads every page, tables, charts and pictures included, and each answer names the pages it used, so you can check it. It's a pnpm monorepo: a React Native app for iOS, Android and web built with One, and a Fastify API over Postgres with pgvector.
techical_contributions: Built document ingestion: Word files go through LibreOffice and Google Docs are fetched as PDFs, then Claude Haiku writes out each page, tables and chart values included, in the background.
Embedded each page with Voyage and stored it in Postgres with pgvector, so a question finds the five pages closest in meaning.
Streamed Claude Sonnet's answers to the app with citations, and showed the part of the page each source used.
Gave each install its own anonymous user through a device id kept in the iOS keychain or Android keystore, and scoped documents and chats to it.
Shared the API types between the server and the app.
non_technical_contributions: Built it to learn how retrieval works end to end, from reading a page to citing it in an answer.
tools_technologies: App: React Native, One, TypeScript, Reanimated
API: Node.js, Fastify, zod
Data: Postgres with pgvector, Postgrator migrations
AI: Claude Haiku to read pages, Claude Sonnet to answer, Voyage embeddings
Tooling: pnpm workspaces, Docker Compose, LibreOffice, Postman
projects.highlight: Answers questions about PDFs, Word files and Google Docs, charts and tables included, and names the page each answer came from
projects.banner_alt: Three iPhone screens: the home screen, an answer citing product-launch.pdf page 2, and the documents list

projects.title: Dosvita
projects.short_description: A web app that turns a CV into a portfolio page: upload a PDF or Word file, Claude extracts it into structured data, and you edit and publish the result. Built with TanStack Start, Supabase and the Claude API, with subscriptions through Paddle.
projects.long_description: Dosvita is my own product, live at dosvita.app. You sign in with Google, upload a CV as a PDF or Word file, and Claude turns it into structured data that becomes a portfolio page you can edit, extend with projects and media, and publish at your own link. Pro plans run through Paddle. I built it end to end, from the Postgres data model to payments.
techical_contributions: Built CV extraction as an Edge Function: reads PDF and Word files, calls Claude with a strict tool schema, and stores the structured result on the portfolio.
Designed the Postgres schema (profiles, CV uploads, portfolios, subscriptions, usage log) with row-level security and locked-down writes.
Integrated Paddle checkout and a signed webhook that keeps subscriptions in sync, and enforced plan limits for portfolios, uploads and media on the server.
Kept a lapsed plan's page online for a while, frozen and with a badge, instead of taking it down straight away.
Added abuse limits on extraction: an in-flight cap, a failure cap, a daily free cap and per-IP limits.
Moved data loading to TanStack Query and kept the Supabase admin client out of the browser bundle.
Added SEO: share cards, structured data, a sitemap, robots and llms.txt.
non_technical_contributions: Came up with the product, named it, and took it from idea to a live, paid product.
Defined the Free and Pro plans, the pricing page, and the terms, privacy and refund pages.
Built it with Claude Code as an AI pair programmer, reviewing every pull request before merging.
tools_technologies: Web app: TanStack Start, TanStack Query, TypeScript in strict mode
UI: Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui
Back end: Supabase (Postgres with row-level security, Google sign-in, Storage, Deno Edge Functions)
AI: the Claude API with strict tool use, plus unpdf and mammoth to read PDF and Word files
Payments: Paddle
Delivery: GitHub Actions, migrations applied by the Supabase GitHub integration
projects.highlight: Live at dosvita.app: a CV in, a published portfolio page out, with paid plans through Paddle
projects.banner_alt: Dosvita in the browser: the home page and an example portfolio

projects.title: Portfolio App
projects.short_description: Picked this portfolio app back up after a roughly two-year gap and rebuilt it end to end using Claude Code as an AI pair programmer, including a full redesign, first-class web support, and a real engineering workflow around it.
projects.long_description: This app, picked back up in August 2026 after about two years. I rebuilt it with Claude Code as an AI pair programmer: I planned the work in Linear, directed the agent session by session, and reviewed every pull request before merging. The tooling around that loop, not just the redesign, became the reusable part.
techical_contributions: Wrote reusable Claude Code skills: commit-conventions (commit, PR and branch naming with Linear ticket IDs), design-handoff-sync (a written design spec into code and a PR, without Figma) and run-expo (launches and drives the app for local checks).
Built the CI pipeline from scratch and set up automated pull request review.
Added first-class web support: pre-rendered pages with their own URL and link preview for every project, a .web.tsx split for web-only layout, and automated deploys to GitHub Pages.
Upgraded Expo SDK 54 to 57 and moved secrets out of source into environment variables.
Moved all content into versioned Supabase migrations, so adding a project, like this one, is a migration.
non_technical_contributions: Scoped the rebuild before any code was written, then broke it into Linear epics, tickets and subtickets.
Planned the "Technical Terminal" redesign: dark, monospace, with a lime accent.
tools_technologies: App: React Native (Expo SDK 57), TypeScript, Expo Router, react-native-web
Content: Supabase (Postgres, PostgREST, row-level security), managed through migrations
AI workflow: Claude Code with custom skills, Linear through its MCP server, the Claude Code GitHub App
Quality: GitHub Actions running TypeScript, oxlint, ESLint, Jest, Knip, a dependency audit and CodeQL, plus Dependabot
Delivery: EAS Update for over-the-air updates, GitHub Pages for the web build
projects.highlight: Every pull request gated by type checks, lint, tests, dead-code detection and CodeQL
projects.banner_alt: mobile-portfolio wordmark under a lime terminal prompt, captioned "Rebuilt with Claude Code"

projects.title: Nectar
projects.short_description: Build and maintain Nectar, a React Native dating application for iOS and Android, owning mobile architecture, typed GraphQL integrations, authentication, subscriptions, notifications, analytics, and releases.
projects.long_description: Nectar is JubileeMedia's dating app for iOS and Android. I set it up from the ground up and own its architecture and delivery: the React Native client, its typed GraphQL layer over Hasura, and the pipeline that ships it through Development, Staging and Production to the App Store and Google Play. I work with the backend and QA teams to validate APIs, investigate data issues and take features from concept to production.
techical_contributions: Organized the app into scalable modules for components, hooks and services, with centralized configuration per environment.
Built CI/CD that automates builds and App Store and Google Play releases.
Made every GraphQL query and mutation fully typed, generated from the schema.
Built sign-in for iOS and Android, and the subscription and payment flows.
Integrated push notifications and in-app messaging across four providers.
Tracked user behavior, conversion funnels and feature performance, and ran A/B tests and staged rollouts.
non_technical_contributions: Catch and clearly document new bugs and issues, making it easier for the whole team to track and prioritize them.
Look for proactive ways to solve problems, often fixing issues directly rather than waiting on someone else.
Explain fixes and reasoning to the team so it helps everyone grow, not just the codebase.
tools_technologies: Client: React Native, Expo, TypeScript
API: GraphQL with Hasura, Apollo Client and GraphQL Code Generator
Auth and payments: Firebase Authentication, RevenueCat
Messaging: Pushwoosh, OneSignal, Firebase, Sendbird
Analytics and rollouts: Mixpanel, Firebase Remote Config
Delivery: Expo, GitHub Actions
projects.highlight: Built and shipped the app that reached 120K monthly active users within 5 months of launch, with 60% D1, 40% D7 and 20% D30 retention
